newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler says EU must escape Blair House oilseed curbs.
newsitem.headline: Fischler says EU must escape Blair House oilseed curbs.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Thursday said that EU oilseed reforms were needed because farmers had reached the limits allowed in the 1992 Blair House pact with Washington.
"The Commission believes it makes sense to opt out of Blair House so that we can grow oilseeds in the future," he told a news conference after a meeting of EU farm ministers.
Fischler added that the planting limits imposed under the Blair House pact would not be practical when 10 east European countries start to join the EU early next century.
The European Commission believes that the Blair House pact would cease to apply if its proposal for a single non-crop specific aid rate was accepted.
Under Blair House, EU-15 oilseed plantings are limited to 5.482 million hectares from which is deducted the current set-aside rate, or a minimum 10 percent.
